days.title: Glacial Lake and Western Shores
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Lago de Sanabria
stops.detail: Lake Sanabria is the most characteristic element of this territory, the largest lake of glacial origin in the Iberian Peninsula, with 318.7 ha and a maximum depth of 53 m.

stops.name: río Tera
stops.detail: The lake is located in the Lake Sanabria Natural Park, and is framed in an exorheic basin where the Tera River constitutes the main water system for entry and exit of the lacustrine system.

days.title: High Peaks and Reservoirs
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Peña Trevinca
stops.detail: The park currently occupies an area of 32,302 ha. which partially or totally affects the municipalities of Galende, Cobreros, Trefacio and Porto, with an altitude that varies between 997 m above sea level on the shores of the lake, up to 2127 m above sea level at the Peña Trevinca peak.

stops.name: embalse de Puente Porto
stops.detail: There are six reservoirs in the lake's hydrographic basin, named: Puente Porto reservoir, Playa reservoir, Cárdena reservoir, Garandones reservoir, Vega de Tera reservoir and Vega de Conde reservoir.
